Build a calendar from a sample of another's timeslices

Source: R/solve_by_sample.R
sample_calendar.Rd

Returns a calendar holding only the chosen timeslices of cal, with the weights that make it annualise: a sample covering half the year weighs each of its slices twice. Used to solve a model, or one of its milestone years, on part of the calendar rather than all of it.

Usage

sample_calendar(cal, slices, counts = NULL, name = "sample")

Arguments

cal

a calendar to sample.

slices

the timeslices to keep. Any level: a leaf set, or coarser members with every finer slice beneath them.

counts

optional named integer vector of repeat counts per timeslice, for a draw with replacement.

name

name for the sampled calendar. A calendar assigned to particular years with setCalendar() needs one, since the horizon refers to it by name.

Value

A calendar covering part of the year, with @year_fraction set to the surviving sum(share).

Details

A sample keeps the parent's timeslice NAMES, its timeframe levels and its share per slice. Only membership and weight change, so a model keyed on the parent's labels still matches, and sum(share * weight) is 1 per level as in any calendar.

At least two members must survive at every level below the year. Dropping a level instead re-derives the leaf names – WIN_h00 becomes h00 – after which the model's data matches nothing and the result solves to zero without complaint. That is refused rather than attempted, naming the level at fault.

counts carries a bootstrap repeat: a slice drawn twice cannot be a repeated row, since a calendar holds each timeslice once, so the repetition becomes a scaled share.

timescales::filter_calendar() is the same operation on a timescales::Calendar, selecting by timeframe and label and recording the parent and the coverage in the object's metadata. This one works on energyRt's own calendar class, which is why it exists separately.

See also

calendar_samples() to plan a set of draws, solve_by_sample() to solve them as replicates, and setCalendar() to give one to particular milestone years.

Examples

cal <- calendars$s4_h24
# two of the four seasons, with every hour beneath them
smp <- sample_calendar(cal, grep("^(WIN|SUM)", cal@timeslice_share$timeslice,
                                 value = TRUE), name = "half")
smp@year_fraction
#> [1] 0.005479452
# share is the parent's; weight annualises
head(smp@timeslice_share, 3)
#>    timeslice       share weight
#>       <char>       <num>  <num>
#> 1:    ANNUAL 1.000000000    1.0
#> 2:       WIN 0.002739726  182.5
#> 3:       SUM 0.002739726  182.5
